Derived from shield_bash_blue, whose printed functional text is byte-identical. Colour variants differ only in {p} and pitch, and both come from card data rather than this file, so the abilities carry over unchanged. Verified against the corpus as its own card. INHERITED NOTE FROM shield_bash_blue: 'If a Guardian off-hand with 1 or more {d} is DEFENDING this chain link, deal 1 damage to the attacking hero unless THEY discard a card.'

Every clause was read off the wrong object. The three conditions were ATTACK_CLASS_IN, ATTACK_SUBTYPE_IN and ATTACK_PITCH_POWER_GTE -- all about the ATTACK, on a card whose sentence is about the DEFENDER, and the third asked about pitch power rather than {d} as well. DEFENDING_CARD_COUNT reads combat.defending_cards and now filters on class and defence too.

The effect was PAY_OR_DAMAGE with amount 1 and an unread 'cost': [DISCARD_CARD]. PAY_OR_DAMAGE reads 'amount' as RESOURCES and defaults damage to 0, and it is entirely self-targeted -- so the card asked its own controller to pay a resource it never mentions, to avoid zero damage, and the discard was dropped. It did nothing at all.

PAY_OR_ELSE is the effect for this sentence shape and already targets a player; it gained discarding as a third currency alongside resources and counters. The choice belongs to the ATTACKING hero, which is why this is not a MAY -- a MAY prompt always goes to the controller, which is how loan_shark_yellow can compose the same wording only because its version is self-targeted.
